post_message: Sabin's Boost Community recently concluded the BoostHER webinar series, a three-part global virtual dialogue spotlighting women’s leadership in immunization and advancing gender-responsive practice across the sector. 🙌  Some key takeaways from these essential conversations:  🔹 Say yes before you feel ready. Women often hold themselves back waiting to feel fully prepared. Stepping into opportunities and learning on the job is how careers accelerate. 🔹 Leadership is a practice, not a position. Regardless of title or role, everyone leads daily through how they show up, communicate, and support others. 🔹 Build a team of mentors, not just one. Different mentors serve different needs. Identify gaps in your skills and goals and find people who speak to each. 🔹 Adaptability is a core leadership skill. The only constant in global health is change. The ability to pivot, learn, and stay flexible determines long-term effectiveness. 🔹 Support other women intentionally. Open doors, make introductions, and lift others up. Collective advancement is a leadership responsibility, not just a personal choice. 🔹 See the full conversation online: https://ow.ly/sbSA50Z9VXv  For even more insights, join the Boost Community — more than 5,000 immunization professionals strong, connecting from around the globe ⤵️ https://ow.ly/xVAl50Z9VXu

post_message: What do a conflict-affected region, an urban slum, and a migrant settlement all have in common?   Turns out, quite a lot.   The new “Social and Behaviour Change to Improve Uptake of Routine Immunization,” a compendium of community-informed and co-designed vaccination interventions from UNICEF, the Sabin Vaccine Institute and Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, looks at innovative community-driven social and behavior change strategies to increase vaccine uptake applied in seven very different settings.  Yet there are some common findings:   • Across all seven countries, trust emerged as the most influential factor in caregiver decision-making. • Access continues to be critical. The most impactful strategies combined targeted SBC interventions with efforts to increase service access, such as mobile clinics, improved referral systems and proactive follow-up.   Sabin’s Senior Manager, Vaccine Demand & Implementation, Theresa Sommers, PhD, MPH, is presenting on the findings this week at UNICEF’s 4th International Social and Behavior Change Communication (SBCC) Summit in Panama. Please connect if you are there!   See the full report ⤵️ https://ow.ly/7vhU50ZfelU
